page: Microsoft Azure E48s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel Xeon 8370C processor cores operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography. The server is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data indicates solid performance across memory and cryptographic operations. The server achieved a PassMark memory score of 2870.18 and a CPU encryption score of 42905.02, both placing in the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 2502.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 160.19 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 67.22 GB/sec. General compute benchmarks, such as the Geekbench multi-core score of 15644.0 and the PassMark CPU score of 48765.22, align with average tier expectations.

While the server demonstrates strong capabilities in image processing and encryption, it exhibits performance limitations on larger computational models. Specifically, LLM text generation using a 70B parameter model is restricted to 2.4 tokens/sec, placing it in the bottom 10% tier due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. However, with 384.0 GB of RAM and average database operation performance of 21815.19 on PassMark, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as relational databases, in-memory caching via Redis, which achieved 44.92 million operations per second, and software compilation.

Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 server lacks local storage and GPUs but supports Premium Storage. Benchmark data highlights strong performance in memory operations and cryptography, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 160.19 GB/sec. Conversely, the lack of GPU acceleration limits heavy AI workloads, as shown by a poor text generation speed of 2.4 tokens/sec on a 70B LLM. The instance is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including relational databases, Redis caching, and large-scale software compilation.
